translation_en:
Emperor Wen, Chengzu, followed this by three times ploughing through their court in punitive campaigns. At that time, it was certainly possible to destroy them before taking the morning meal. Yet imperial benevolence, encompassing all like Heaven, allowed them a breathing space. Now the surviving evildoers have multiplied and spread, troubling our frontiers. Fortunately, our Emperor, intelligent and possessed of divine martial prowess, carries forward the achievements of the two sagely ancestors. With awe-inspiring resolve, he has commanded generals to take the field, appointed a censorial official as Supreme Commander to unify authority, and selected a tiger-like general with independent field command to direct the troops. The Minister of Revenue has disbursed money and grain in immense quantities; the Minister of Works has repeatedly issued strict instructions concerning military equipment. In his unremitting attention to subduing the barbarians, His Majesty has surely settled his plans and made his decisions firmly.

Thus his sagely martial might has shone forth far and wide, and two years have already passed without alarm on the frontiers. Yet the intentions of the Rong are unfathomable, and their appearances and disappearances follow no regular pattern. To withdraw our defenses would leave us unprepared for the unexpected, while maintaining them entails toil and expense: these are indeed concerns such as you have raised. Considering the present situation, however, we must make defense our means of warfare. Even where this entails toil and expense, there are things we cannot afford to begrudge. Why? This is what I mean by making our precautions stringent.

Moreover, Su Xun once said: “The general principle of warfare is this: before battle, nurture strength; when battle is imminent, nurture spirit; after battle, nurture financial resources.” Once fighting is over, one might expect there to be nothing further to attend to; yet he still wished to nurture financial resources. Was this not precisely to maintain stringent preparations and make defense a means of warfare? Now, …

title: 嘉靖二十三年會試錄
text:
欲以守而為戰則養財之道舍屯田鹽法
之外亦無可講矣何也昔趙充國之留屯
湟中韓重華之墾田代北是皆以守而為
戰者也而其迹皆在今山陜之域顧今皆
鞠而為莽矣況夫近日五堡之復可以廣
新屯
國初河西之屯可以尋舊績是亦不可以復
講矣乎且管敬仲之佐齊也以鹽筴而致
霸劉晏通兩淮之鹺而唐之中興寔賴之
===
今之法固猶夫法也而文具則多矣況夫
餘鹽之榷可轉而給邊私鹽之逸可收以
佐餉是又可以弗講乎或謂今鹽法尚可
理而屯田則未易以復者然則今之勞且
費將終不能以有濟乎無已則有簡兵之
說乎愚聞之兵貴精不貴多兵多則冗徒
足以耗食今之兵方患其不多而顧又苦
其冗何也弗簡之故也無多之名而有冗
之實所以坐耗其食而弗知也且兵無事

欲以守而爲戰則養財之道舍屯田鹽法

今之法固猶夫法也而文具則多矣况夫
餘鹽之榷可轉而給邊私鹽之逸可收以
佐餉是又可以弗講乎或謂今鹽法尚可
理而屯田則未易以復者然則今之勞且
費將終不能以有濟乎無已則有簡兵之
說乎愚聞之兵貴精不貴多兵多則冗徒
足以耗食今之兵方患其不多而顧又苦
其冗何也弗簡之故也無多之名而有冗
之實所以坐耗其食而弗知也且兵無事
punctuated:
欲以守而為戰，則養財之道，舍屯田鹽法之外，亦無可講矣。何也？昔趙充國之留屯湟中，韓重華之墾田代北，是皆以守而為戰者也，而其迹皆在今山陜之域，顧今皆鞠而為莽矣。況夫近日五堡之復，可以廣新屯；國初河西之屯，可以尋舊績。是亦不可以復講矣乎？且管敬仲之佐齊也，以鹽筴而致霸；劉晏通兩淮之鹺，而唐之中興寔賴之。今之法固猶夫法也，而文具則多矣。況夫餘鹽之榷，可轉而給邊；私鹽之逸，可收以佐餉。是又可以弗講乎？

或謂今鹽法尚可理，而屯田則未易以復者。然則今之勞且費，將終不能以有濟乎？無已，則有簡兵之說乎？愚聞之，兵貴精，不貴多；兵多則冗，徒足以耗食。今之兵，方患其不多，而顧又苦其冗，何也？弗簡之故也。無多之名，而有冗之實，所以坐耗其食而弗知也。且兵無事……
translation_en:
…If defense is to serve as warfare, then, as means of sustaining financial resources, there is nothing to discuss beyond military agricultural colonies and the salt administration. Why is this? In former times, Zhao Chongguo kept troops to cultivate land in Huangzhong, and Han Chonghua reclaimed fields north of Dai. Both used defense as warfare, and the sites of their achievements all lie within present-day Shanxi and Shaanxi. Yet now these have all become wilderness. Moreover, the recent recovery of the Five Forts offers an opportunity to expand new military agricultural colonies, while the colonies established in Hexi at the beginning of our dynasty offer earlier achievements that can be traced and renewed. Should these matters not be taken up again? Furthermore, when Guan Jingzhong assisted Qi, he brought it to hegemony through his salt policy. Liu Yan facilitated the salt trade of the Two Huai regions, and the Tang restoration truly depended upon it. Today's regulations are still those same regulations, but much has become mere paperwork. Moreover, revenue from the monopoly on surplus salt could be transferred to provision the frontier, and the proceeds now escaping through illicit salt could be recovered to supplement military supplies. Can these matters go undiscussed?

Some say that the salt administration can still be put in order today, but that military agricultural colonies cannot readily be restored. Does this mean that our present toil and expenditure will ultimately accomplish nothing? If there is no other course, might we consider selecting the troops? I have heard that what matters in troops is quality, not numbers. When troops are numerous, they become superfluous and merely consume provisions. Today we worry that our troops are too few, yet also suffer from their redundancy. Why is this? It is because they have not been carefully selected. Without being reputed numerous, they are in fact redundant; hence they idly consume provisions, and we fail to recognize it. Moreover, when troops have no duties…

title: 嘉靖二十三年會試錄
text:
而食則不可使聚聚則不可使無事而食
此二者相勝而不可以並行是故以守為
戰之兵尤不可不簡也是非愚言也倡勇
敢練材實蘇軾盖嘗言之矣亦非徒軾言
也募驍勇飭訓練李抱真盖嘗行之矣今
誠能倣而行之練之既精蓄之既豫於是
乎隸之以屯田有事則戰無事則耕是簡
兵者乃所以益兵也以是而守而亦何勞
且費之足慮乎哉愚書生也而談兵知必
===
見迂矣然而不敢嘿也謹以是復
alt_text:
此二者相勝而不可以並行是故以守爲
戰之兵尤不可不簡也是非愚言也倡勇
敢練材實蘇軾蓋嘗言之矣亦非徒軾言
也募驍勇飭訓練李抱真蓋嘗行之矣今
誠能倣而行之練之既精蓄之既豫於是
乎隸之以屯田有事則戰無事則耕是簡
兵者乃所以益兵也以是而守而亦何勞
且費之足慮乎哉愚書生也而談兵知必
===
見迂矣然而不敢嘿也謹以是復
punctuated: 而食，則不可使聚；聚，則不可使無事而食。此二者相勝，而不可以並行。是故以守為戰之兵，尤不可不簡也。是非愚言也，倡勇敢，練材實，蘇軾盖嘗言之矣；亦非徒軾言也，募驍勇，飭訓練，李抱真盖嘗行之矣。今誠能倣而行之，練之既精，蓄之既豫，於是乎隸之以屯田，有事則戰，無事則耕，是簡兵者乃所以益兵也。以是而守，而亦何勞且費之足慮乎哉？愚書生也，而談兵，知必見迂矣；然而不敢嘿也，謹以是復。
translation_en: …and draw provisions, they must not be allowed to congregate; if they congregate, they must not be allowed to draw provisions while idle. These two conditions work against one another and cannot operate together. Thus troops whose warfare consists in defense must above all be carefully selected. These are not merely my own words: Su Shi indeed once advocated encouraging the brave and training men of real ability. Nor did this remain mere talk on Su Shi’s part: Li Baozhen indeed once put into practice the recruitment of valiant men and the rigorous enforcement of training. If today we could truly follow these examples, once the troops were thoroughly trained and provisions laid up in advance, we could assign them to military agricultural colonies. When there was fighting to be done, they would fight; when there was none, they would farm. Thus selecting troops is precisely the means of strengthening the army. With such troops defending our borders, what toil and expense would there be to worry about? I am but a scholar, yet I venture to discuss military affairs, knowing that I shall surely be regarded as impractical. Nevertheless, I dare not remain silent, and respectfully submit this reply.

translation_en:
Afterword to the Record of the Metropolitan Examination

In the twenty-third year of His Majesty’s reign, the Metropolitan Examination was held for scholars from throughout the realm. His Majesty thereupon commanded your servant Rubi, Left Mentor, to preside over the examination. Your servant Zan and the others, by virtue of our official duties, were undeservedly appointed Associate Examiners. We were filled with trepidation, fearing that we could not adequately fulfill His Majesty’s benevolent intentions. Once the work was completed, a record was compiled for presentation to the throne. I was again called upon, for want of someone better, to obey His Majesty’s illustrious command and write an afterword on its concluding leaves. The selection of officials is a great institutional undertaking; reverently proclaiming His Majesty’s intentions and disseminating them throughout the realm is a weighty commission. Your servant therefore respectfully bows with clasped hands and touches his forehead to the ground, proclaiming these words:

Your servant considers: is the transformation and perfection of the realm through cultural refinement attested by the flourishing of cosmic forces and fortune? From the beginning of remote antiquity, cultural refinement…

title: 嘉靖二十三年會試錄
text:
肇而未鬯聖王繼作神化之
道日以昭著而至堯為獨盛
故曰堯得天地中數茲非氣
運之隆乎維時翊運之臣若
宅百揆典禮樂平水土教樹
藝濟濟師師罔不承化輔理
以共迓雍熙之治何其盛也
===
我
國家汛掃胡元闢乾坤而再造
之豈直曰繼作已哉百七十
餘年
聖聖相承重熙累洽貞元文明之
會寔維其期
皇上應運中興作民

translation_en:
…had begun to emerge but had not yet fully flourished. Sage kings arose in succession, and the Way of wondrous transformation became more manifest each day, reaching its greatest flourishing under Yao. Thus it is said: “Yao attained the central measure of Heaven and Earth.” Was this not a culmination of cosmic fortune? At that time, ministers who assisted the unfolding of this fortune—whether overseeing the hundred offices, administering rites and music, regulating waters and lands, or teaching planting and cultivation—were numerous and dignified, taking one another as models. All carried forward the transforming influence and assisted in governance, together ushering in harmonious and prosperous rule. How flourishing it was!
Our dynasty swept away the alien Yuan, opened Heaven and Earth anew, and created them afresh. How could this be called merely another succession of rulers? For more than 170 years, sage sovereigns have succeeded one another, accumulating prosperity and concord. This indeed was the appointed time for a conjunction of cyclical renewal and cultural brilliance. His Majesty, responding to cosmic fortune, has brought about a restoration and become the people's…

translation_en:
…as ruler and teacher. His grand plans and mighty achievements shine throughout heaven and earth and stand resplendent across past and present; they cannot readily be recounted in full. As for his Admonition on Reverent Oneness and his annotations on the Five Admonitions, all under Heaven vie to transmit and recite them. The method of cultivating the mind embodied therein profoundly grasps the essence of the transmission handed down since Yao.

Thus the transforming influence of the Way flows abundantly, and cultural instruction spreads far and wide. After long immersion in this influence and its inspiration, all within and beyond the seas submit and obey. Even insects, plants, and trees may hope to receive his abundant beneficence and be bathed in his radiance; how much more, then, those who serve together as the Emperor’s subjects? Thus transformation through human culture flourishes most abundantly in this age, attesting to the flourishing fortunes of the times. You scholars have been born to encounter…

title: 嘉靖二十三年會試錄
text:
聖世千載一時乃今登名茲錄且
將奉
大對於
聖天子之庭矣繼自今其尚精白
乃心服乃政展采錯事以共
弼我
明無疆之駿烈不知亦有如堯之
===
時九官十二牧者出於其間
否乎夫仕也難進而易退時
也難得而易失有其時矣乃
或罔知自効卑卑焉如庸衆
所爲甚至靜言庸違物遷而
渝其初斯敝臣矣豈徒負
君將不負於時乎臣用是大懼於

punctuated: 聖世，千載一時，乃今登名茲錄，且將奉大對於聖天子之庭矣。繼自今，其尚精白乃心，服乃政，展采錯事，以共弼我明無疆之駿烈。不知亦有如堯之時九官十二牧者出於其間否乎？夫仕也，難進而易退；時也，難得而易失。有其時矣，乃或罔知自効，卑卑焉如庸衆所爲，甚至靜言庸違，物遷而渝其初，斯敝臣矣！豈徒負君，將不負於時乎？臣用是大懼於
translation_en:
…in this sagely age, an opportunity encountered once in a thousand years, you now have your names entered in this record and will soon offer your answers at the Palace Examination in the court of the sagely Son of Heaven. From this time forward, may you purify your hearts, discharge your governmental duties, display your abilities, and carry out your tasks, together assisting our Ming dynasty in its boundless, magnificent achievements. Might men like the nine officers and twelve regional governors of Yao’s time also emerge from among you?

Entering office is difficult, while withdrawing is easy; the opportune moment is difficult to obtain and easy to lose. Having obtained that opportunity, some may nevertheless fail to understand how to render service, behaving in petty fashion like the common run of men. They may even speak fair words while acting contrary to them, abandoning their original purpose as circumstances change. Such men are unworthy ministers! Would they merely be failing their sovereign? Would they not also be failing the age? For this reason, your servant feels profound apprehension concerning…

聖天子之
寵命
翰林院修撰儒林郎茅瓚謹

punctuated:
諸士始進，敢申告而胥飭之，期無負於明時，庶幾以對揚聖天子之寵命。
翰林院修撰、儒林郎茅瓚謹序。
translation_en:
…as you gentlemen first enter official service, I venture to offer these admonitions and urge you all to diligence, hoping that you will not fail this enlightened age and may thereby fittingly acknowledge and give lustre to the sagely Son of Heaven’s gracious command.
Preface respectfully composed by Mao Zan, Senior Compiler in the Hanlin Academy, with the prestige title Gentleman for the Forest of Scholars.
